script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. Monday — here is your MEME recap. The portfolio closed up nine point six nine percent on the session. Across nine primary holdings, every single name finished green. That does not happen often.

Applied Optoelectronics surged as much as seventeen point six percent intraday, closing the session with a sixteen point eight five percent gain. Earnings are due, and the market is already pricing in something significant.

The broad market caught a strong bid on Monday after President Donald Trump signaled a willingness to restart nuclear talks with Iran, fueling hopes of a Middle East ceasefire and unlocking risk appetite across sectors. The Nasdaq led the advance, with artificial intelligence infrastructure names among the primary beneficiaries. No Federal Reserve commentary or major economic prints crossed during the session.

Applied Optoelectronics is the top story today, and the numbers demand attention. The stock closed up sixteen point eight five percent, with intraday highs touching an eighteen percent gain. The catalyst is straightforward: investors are repositioning ahead of what analysts expect to be a blowout second quarter. Revenue is projected to grow between seventy-five and ninety-two percent year over year. According to commentary aggregated by Yahoo Finance, three structural forces are converging — clearing a critical threshold in optical networking complexity, accelerating data center demand tied to artificial intelligence buildouts, and a credible path toward a potential billion-dollar revenue year. This is a seven point four three percent position in the portfolio, the largest single holding. Momentum is firmly intact. The next hard gate is the earnings report itself. Any shortfall against elevated expectations carries meaningful downside risk, but for now, the market is voting with conviction.

Applied Optoelectronics, as covered, was up sixteen point eight five percent on the session. The position leads the portfolio by weight and led Monday's performance by price action. Watch the earnings print closely — this stock is priced for perfection heading in.

Turning to Redwire Corporation, up eleven point eight three percent. Yahoo Finance published a pair of comparative pieces Monday, stacking Redwire against both Advance Auto Parts and Rocket Lab. The framing is instructive: Redwire is characterized as a high-growth space contractor still burning cash, but one with a differentiated satellite components business. Competitive positioning relative to Rocket Lab will remain a recurring narrative into year-end.

Over at Nebius Group, up eleven point six four percent on the session. Seeking Alpha identified the company as the lead neocloud operator, citing vertical infrastructure integration, a strategic partnership with Nvidia, and industry-leading revenue growth visibility. A broader risk-on rotation in artificial intelligence cloud stocks — including CoreWeave, Snowflake, and Oracle — amplified the move. Nebius represents a six point zero one percent position and remains a direct beneficiary of sustained enterprise artificial intelligence spending.

AST SpaceMobile gained seven point seven zero percent. The picture heading into earnings next week is mixed. Seeking Alpha noted the company has secured three point eight billion dollars in liquidity and maintained its one hundred fifty to two hundred million dollar revenue guidance for the full year. However, Yahoo Finance flagged that consensus expectations suggest the company does not currently carry the right setup for an earnings beat. That tension is worth monitoring closely.

Bloom Energy was up six point zero eight percent. Seeking Alpha highlighted an impressive setup: second-quarter revenues came in at one point zero seven billion dollars, representing a one hundred sixty-five percent increase year over year, with gross margins exceeding thirty-three percent. A separate piece noted the stock remains down thirty-eight percent from its fifty-two-week high, which frames the current level as a potential recovery entry for longer-term holders.

Meanwhile, TeraWulf added six point six three percent on the session. No company-specific news drove the move. The gain tracks in line with the broader technology and digital infrastructure rally seen across the session. The next meaningful catalyst will be any update on hash rate expansion or energy cost structure.

Lumentum Holdings climbed nine point two four percent. The advance fits a sector-wide pattern — optical networking names moved sharply higher Monday. Yahoo Finance noted that Corning, a peer, gained six point five percent after analysts described its recent pullback as a more reasonable entry point. Lumentum carries similar exposure to the artificial intelligence data center infrastructure buildout and benefited from that same tailwind.

IREN Limited was up eight point zero two percent. Like TeraWulf, the move reflects sector momentum rather than a discrete news catalyst. Digital infrastructure and compute-adjacent names tracked higher across the board, consistent with the risk-on session.

Sandisk Corporation closed up six point zero three percent. Yahoo Finance cited a broad market rally linked to the Trump Iran comments as lifting names across the technology complex, with Micron specifically mentioned as a memory sector beneficiary. Sandisk trades with similar exposure to memory market dynamics.

Three data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, AST SpaceMobile reports earnings next week — the specific date confirmation will matter for positioning. Second, Applied Optoelectronics earnings are imminent — the revenue range of seventy-five to ninety-two percent growth sets a high bar. Third, any follow-through on Middle East ceasefire developments could sustain or reverse Monday's broad risk-on bid across the portfolio.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch for any pre-earnings guidance revisions out of Applied Optoelectronics and whether the artificial intelligence cloud rotation sustains or fades into Tuesday's open.
